content.text:
Option 2, the one with the line of plain Hebrew under each index name. Fairly sure. What decided it: under S&P 500 it says "חמש מאות החברות הגדולות בארצות הברית", so I finally get what I'd actually be buying. In option 1, "ת"א-125" and "MSCI AC World" are just names to me.

**How I went through it:**
- **Screen 1:** I saw the heading "קרנות סל" and "4 קרנות", then went down the fund names. I stopped on S&P 500 because that's what the guys at work talk about. I looked at the fees on the left and saw three numbers per fund: "קבוע", "משתנה", "נאמן". I don't know if I'm supposed to add them up, or which one is the real fee.
- **Screen 2:** It's the same table but with a description under each index. I read the S&P one ("חמש מאות החברות הגדולות בארצות הברית"), the 125 one ("מאה עשרים וחמש החברות... בתל אביב") and the world one ("מניות חברות בשווקים מפותחים ומתפתחים"). After that it clicked: two Israeli funds, one American, one whole world.
- The fees look the same in both. In both, the S&P fund looks the most expensive (0.8% and 0.3%, against 0.1% and 0.1% for the 90 fund). It's still just percent, so it doesn't feel like much money.

**What I skipped:**
- The grey line at the top ("רק הקרנות שהאתר אסף עליהן דוח...").
- The fund numbers 1148808 and so on.
- The "בדף הקרן במאיה" links.
- I didn't tap any of the underlined fee numbers either.

**Words I didn't get:**
- "נאמן"
- "צוברת"
- "עסקת החלף"
- "קבוע" / "משתנה", in the sense of which one I actually pay
- "(4A)" / "(4D)"
- "מחזיקה את המניות", which only sort of made sense
- "חשיפה לדולר"

**What bothered me:**
- "מס גם על שינויי המטבע" on the S&P and world funds. Tax on top? That kind of puts me off the very fund I came for.
- "עסקת החלף" sounds like some trick.
- In option 2 those tags drop onto a second line, so the tax one stands out even more.
- Nowhere does it say how much I'd pay in shekels on my 30,000.
- Nothing says which one is better for someone like me, or what to do first. I'd leave knowing what each fund holds, but I still wouldn't buy anything today.
